test_layout: 12 tests per task in order easy,medium,hard repeated 4 times; tests 1-6 = visible pool, tests 7-12 = hidden set
notes: Prompts name the standard but do not list its rules. Tasks with a 'forbid' field must not import the listed modules (runner.py checks this automatically). Needs the updated runner.py.

tasks.title: SHA-256 from scratch
tasks.signature: def sha256_hex(data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `sha256_hex(data_hex)` returning the SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) digest of the bytes in `data_hex` as lower-case hex. Implement the algorithm yourself: do not import hashlib, hmac or any library that computes hashes. Raise `ValueError` if `data_hex` is not strict hex (even length, digits 0-9 and a-f in either case).

tasks.title: SHA-512 from scratch
tasks.signature: def sha512_hex(data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `sha512_hex(data_hex)` returning the SHA-512 (FIPS 180-4) digest of the bytes in `data_hex` as lower-case hex. Implement the algorithm yourself: do not import hashlib, hmac or any library that computes hashes. Raise `ValueError` if `data_hex` is not strict hex (even length, digits 0-9 and a-f in either case).

tasks.title: SHA3-256 from scratch
tasks.signature: def sha3_256_hex(data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `sha3_256_hex(data_hex)` returning the SHA3-256 (FIPS 202) digest of the bytes in `data_hex` as lower-case hex. Implement Keccak yourself: do not import hashlib, hmac or any library that computes hashes. Raise `ValueError` if `data_hex` is not strict hex (even length, digits 0-9 and a-f in either case).

tasks.title: SHAKE128 from scratch
tasks.signature: def shake128_hex(data_hex: str, outlen: int) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `shake128_hex(data_hex, outlen)` returning `outlen` bytes of SHAKE128 (FIPS 202) output for the bytes in `data_hex`, as lower-case hex. Implement Keccak yourself: do not import hashlib, hmac or any library that computes hashes. Raise `ValueError` if `data_hex` is not strict hex or `outlen` is not an int from 1 to 2000 (a bool does not count).

tasks.title: BLAKE2b-256 from scratch
tasks.signature: def blake2b256_hex(data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `blake2b256_hex(data_hex)` returning the unkeyed BLAKE2b (RFC 7693) digest with a 32-byte output for the bytes in `data_hex`, as lower-case hex. Implement the algorithm yourself: do not import hashlib, hmac or any library that computes hashes. Raise `ValueError` if `data_hex` is not strict hex (even length, digits 0-9 and a-f in either case).

tasks.title: HMAC from the hash function (4 algorithms)
tasks.signature: def hmac_hex(algo: str, key_hex: str, msg_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `hmac_hex(algo, key_hex, msg_hex)` returning the HMAC (RFC 2104) of the message under the key, as lower-case hex, for `algo` one of `sha256`, `sha384`, `sha512`, `sha3_256`. Build it yourself from the hash function: you may use hashlib for the hash, but do not import hmac. Raise `ValueError` for any other algorithm name or invalid hex.

tasks.title: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 from scratch
tasks.signature: def pbkdf2_sha512_hex(password: str, salt_hex: str, iterations: int, dklen: int) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `pbkdf2_sha512_hex(password, salt_hex, iterations, dklen)` returning PBKDF2 (RFC 8018) with HMAC-SHA-512 as lower-case hex, for the UTF-8 password. Implement PBKDF2 and HMAC yourself using only `hashlib.sha512`: do not import hmac and do not call hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac, hashlib.scrypt or hashlib.new. Raise `ValueError` unless the salt is strict hex, `iterations` is an int from 1 to 1000000 and `dklen` an int from 1 to 1024 (bools do not count).

tasks.title: AES block encryption from scratch
tasks.signature: def aes_encrypt_block(key_hex: str, block_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `aes_encrypt_block(key_hex, block_hex)` that encrypts one 16-byte block with AES (FIPS 197) and returns the 16 bytes as lower-case hex. The key may be 128, 192 or 256 bits. Implement AES yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` for any other key length, a block that is not 16 bytes, or hex that is not strict.

tasks.title: AES-CTR from scratch
tasks.signature: def aes_ctr_hex(key_hex: str, counter_hex: str, data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `aes_ctr_hex(key_hex, counter_hex, data_hex)` that encrypts (or decrypts) the data with AES in CTR mode (NIST SP 800-38A) and returns lower-case hex. `counter_hex` is the 16-byte initial counter block; the whole block is incremented as a big-endian integer for every 16 bytes of data. Keys may be 128, 192 or 256 bits. Implement AES yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` for a bad key length, a counter that is not 16 bytes, or hex that is not strict.

tasks.title: AES-CBC with PKCS#7 from scratch
tasks.signature: def aes_cbc_encrypt_hex(key_hex: str, iv_hex: str, data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `aes_cbc_encrypt_hex(key_hex, iv_hex, data_hex)` that pads the data with PKCS#7 and encrypts it with AES in CBC mode, returning lower-case hex. The key may be 128, 192 or 256 bits and the IV is 16 bytes. Implement AES yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` for a bad key length, an IV that is not 16 bytes, or hex that is not strict.

tasks.title: AES-GCM from scratch
tasks.signature: def aes_gcm_encrypt_hex(key_hex: str, iv_hex: str, aad_hex: str, data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `aes_gcm_encrypt_hex(key_hex, iv_hex, aad_hex, data_hex)` that encrypts with AES-GCM (NIST SP 800-38D) and returns the ciphertext followed by the 16-byte tag as lower-case hex. The key may be 128, 192 or 256 bits and the IV must be exactly 12 bytes. Implement AES and GHASH yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` for a bad key length, an IV that is not 12 bytes, or hex that is not strict.

tasks.title: Poly1305 from scratch
tasks.signature: def poly1305_hex(key_hex: str, msg_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `poly1305_hex(key_hex, msg_hex)` that returns the Poly1305 one-time authenticator (RFC 8439) of the message under a 32-byte key, as lower-case hex. Implement it yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` if the key is not 32 bytes or either hex text is not strict hex.

tasks.title: ChaCha20 from scratch
tasks.signature: def chacha20_xor_hex(key_hex: str, nonce_hex: str, counter: int, data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `chacha20_xor_hex(key_hex, nonce_hex, counter, data_hex)` that encrypts (or decrypts) the data with ChaCha20 as in RFC 8439 (32-byte key, 12-byte nonce, 32-bit block counter starting at `counter`) and returns lower-case hex. Implement it yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` for a bad key or nonce length, non-hex input, a counter that is not an int from 0 to 2**32-1 (a bool does not count), or data so long that the block counter would pass 2**32-1.

tasks.title: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD from scratch
tasks.signature: def chacha20poly1305_encrypt_hex(key_hex: str, nonce_hex: str, aad_hex: str, data_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `chacha20poly1305_encrypt_hex(key_hex, nonce_hex, aad_hex, data_hex)` that encrypts with the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD of RFC 8439 (32-byte key, 12-byte nonce) and returns the ciphertext followed by the 16-byte tag as lower-case hex. Implement ChaCha20 and Poly1305 yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` for a bad key or nonce length or hex that is not strict.

tasks.title: X25519 key exchange from scratch
tasks.signature: def x25519_hex(scalar_hex: str, u_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `x25519_hex(scalar_hex, u_hex)` that computes X25519 as specified in RFC 7748 for a 32-byte scalar and a 32-byte u-coordinate (both little-endian hex) and returns the 32-byte result as lower-case hex. Implement it yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` if an input is not exactly 32 bytes of strict hex, or if the result is all zeros.

tasks.title: Ed25519 public key from a seed
tasks.signature: def ed25519_public_key_hex(seed_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `ed25519_public_key_hex(seed_hex)` that derives the Ed25519 (RFC 8032) public key from a 32-byte seed and returns the 32-byte encoded point as lower-case hex. You may use `hashlib.sha512`, but implement the curve arithmetic yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` if the seed is not exactly 32 bytes of strict hex.

tasks.title: secp256k1 public key from a private key
tasks.signature: def secp256k1_pubkey_compressed(priv_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `secp256k1_pubkey_compressed(priv_hex)` that returns the compressed SEC1 public key (33 bytes, lower-case hex) of a secp256k1 private key given as exactly 64 hex digits. Implement the curve arithmetic yourself: do not import any cryptography library. Raise `ValueError` if the text is not exactly 64 hex digits or the key is not in the valid range.

tasks.title: Modular square root
tasks.signature: def sqrt_mod(a: int, p: int) -> int
tasks.prompt: Write `sqrt_mod(a, p)` that returns the smallest non-negative integer r with r*r congruent to `a` modulo the prime `p` (a is reduced modulo p first; for a = 0 the answer is 0). Raise `ValueError` if `p` is not a prime, if `a` is not a square modulo `p`, or if an argument is not an int (a bool does not count). It must work for primes of 256 bits and more.

tasks.title: Chinese remainder theorem (any moduli)
tasks.signature: def crt(residues: list[int], moduli: list[int]) -> list[int]
tasks.prompt: Write `crt(residues, moduli)` that solves the system x = residues[i] (mod moduli[i]) and returns `[x, m]` where m is the least common multiple of the moduli and 0 <= x < m. The moduli need not be coprime, and residues may be negative or larger than their modulus. Raise `ValueError` if the lists are empty or of different lengths, if a modulus is below 1, if an entry is not an int (a bool does not count), or if the system has no solution.

tasks.title: Integer factorization (64-bit)
tasks.signature: def factorize(n: int) -> list[int]
tasks.prompt: Write `factorize(n)` that returns the prime factors of `n` in ascending order, repeated according to their multiplicity (so 12 gives [2, 2, 3]). It must handle every `n` from 2 to 2**64 - 1, each within about a second. Raise `ValueError` for any other int, or if `n` is not an int (a bool does not count).

tasks.title: Discrete logarithm modulo a prime
tasks.signature: def discrete_log(g: int, h: int, p: int) -> int
tasks.prompt: Write `discrete_log(g, h, p)` that returns the smallest x >= 0 with g**x congruent to h modulo the prime p, where 1 <= g, h < p and p < 2**41. It must finish within a few seconds for primes of 40 bits. Raise `ValueError` if there is no such x, if p is not a prime, if an argument is out of range, or if an argument is not an int (a bool does not count).

tasks.title: Exact integer k-th root
tasks.signature: def integer_root(n: int, k: int) -> int
tasks.prompt: Write `integer_root(n, k)` that returns the largest integer r with r**k <= n, exactly, for arbitrarily large `n` (thousands of digits). Do not use floating point. Raise `ValueError` if `n` is negative, `k` is below 1, or an argument is not an int (a bool does not count).

tasks.title: ECDSA DER signature to raw r||s
tasks.signature: def ecdsa_der_to_raw(der_hex: str, size: int) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `ecdsa_der_to_raw(der_hex, size)` converting a hex-encoded DER ECDSA signature into the fixed-width raw r||s form (IEEE P1363), each value `size` bytes, as lower-case hex. Raise `ValueError` for anything that is not a strictly valid DER signature, or whose r or s does not fit in `size` bytes.

tasks.title: TLS 1.3 HKDF-Expand-Label
tasks.signature: def hkdf_expand_label_hex(secret_hex: str, label: str, context_hex: str, length: int) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `hkdf_expand_label_hex(secret_hex, label, context_hex, length)` implementing HKDF-Expand-Label from TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446) with SHA-256, returning the output as lower-case hex. Do not use hashlib's hkdf-like helpers or crypto packages beyond hmac and hashlib. Raise `ValueError` for bad hex or for parameters the construction cannot encode.

tasks.title: Generic parametrised CRC
tasks.signature: def crc_hex(data_hex: str, width: int, poly: int, init: int, refin: bool, refout: bool, xorout: int) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `crc_hex(data_hex, width, poly, init, refin, refout, xorout)` computing a CRC in the Rocksoft model for any width from 1 to 64 bits over the bytes of `data_hex`. Return the result as lower-case hex zero-padded to ceil(width/8) bytes. Implement it yourself (no zlib, binascii or CRC packages). Raise `ValueError` for bad hex or out-of-range parameters.

tasks.title: Bech32 / Bech32m decoder
tasks.signature: def bech32_decode(text: str) -> list
tasks.prompt: Write `bech32_decode(text)` returning `[hrp, data, spec]`, where `hrp` is the lower-case human-readable part, `data` is the list of 5-bit values without the checksum, and `spec` is `"bech32"` or `"bech32m"`. Follow BIP 173 and BIP 350, and raise `ValueError` for any invalid string.

tasks.title: Base58Check decoder
tasks.signature: def base58check_decode(text: str) -> list
tasks.prompt: Write `base58check_decode(text)` for Bitcoin-style Base58Check strings. Return `[version_hex, payload_hex]` where the first decoded byte is the version and the 4-byte checksum is removed. Raise `ValueError` for any invalid string.

tasks.title: SCRAM-SHA-256 client proof
tasks.signature: def scram_client_proof(password: str, client_first_bare: str, server_first: str, client_final_no_proof: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `scram_client_proof(password, client_first_bare, server_first, client_final_no_proof)` returning the base64 ClientProof of SCRAM-SHA-256 (RFC 5802 / RFC 7677). Salt and iteration count come from `server_first`. Raise `ValueError` if `server_first` is malformed, its nonce does not continue the client nonce, or the iteration count is not a positive integer.

tasks.title: RFC 6979 deterministic nonce (P-256)
tasks.signature: def rfc6979_k_p256(priv_hex: str, msg_hex: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `rfc6979_k_p256(priv_hex, msg_hex)` returning, as 64 lower-case hex digits, the deterministic ECDSA nonce k of RFC 6979 for curve P-256 with SHA-256, private key `priv_hex` and message `msg_hex` (the message is hashed with SHA-256 inside). Raise `ValueError` for bad hex or a private key outside the valid range.

tasks.title: JWK thumbprint
tasks.signature: def jwk_thumbprint(jwk_json: str) -> str
tasks.prompt: Write `jwk_thumbprint(jwk_json)` returning the RFC 7638 SHA-256 thumbprint of a JSON Web Key given as a JSON string, as unpadded base64url. Raise `ValueError` for invalid JSON or a key that cannot be thumbprinted.
